answer_raw.explanation: The yield drop began right after a cleaning-protocol change and new yeast-propagation batch, and batches smelled sour — classic signs of bacterial (e.g. lactic/acetic) contamination outcompeting yeast, not underfeeding or low temperature. Direct contamination assays (lactic acid, bacterial count, pH) were not available in this system, so I tested the hypothesis by intervention. Dosing the antimicrobial hop extract produced a clean dose-response in EthanolYield: dose 0 ~ -9 (worst), 25 -> +2, 50 -> +18.7, 75 -> +26.4, 100 -> +26.5 — a monotonic rise to a plateau around dose 75, confirming a suppressible microbial burden was causing the loss. The team's favored levers were decoys: increasing sugar feed did not raise yield (contradicting the underfeed theory), and adding antifoam changed the BrothFoaming reading without improving yield (foaming is a bystander). DissolvedO2 also does not track the true cause. Recommended fix: dose antimicrobial hop extract at ~75 (full benefit reached; 100 gives no extra gain, so avoid overdosing) and, at the source, review the changed cleaning protocol and new yeast propagation batch as the likely contamination entry point.
